fieldMarks: Large semi-aquatic rodent, body 47–61 cm plus a 37–41 cm tail; up to about 9 kg
Light to dark brown fur; long, round, sparsely haired tail
Conspicuous white whiskers and prominent incisors on a large, nearly triangular head
First four toes of the hind feet webbed, the fifth free
behavior: Mostly nocturnal, peaking near midnight; more daytime activity when food is scarce
Digs out roots, rhizomes and tubers with its forepaws, especially in winter; occasionally eats mussels and crustaceans
Feeds in the emergent-vegetation zone of wetlands
habitat: Fresh marshes preferred, but also bayous, rivers, impoundments, farm ponds, canals, swamps and brackish or salt coastal marshes.
range: Native to southern South America. Introduced in Louisiana in the 1930s and spread widely; now in the southeastern and south-central U.S., Oregon, Washington, Maryland and other states, with records in British Columbia.

lookalikes.name: Beaver
lookalikes.howToTell: Beavers have a broad flat tail and fully webbed hind feet.

lookalikes.name: Muskrat
lookalikes.howToTell: Muskrats are much smaller with a short side-flattened tail and unwebbed toes.
